title: Yang–Mills connections on Euclidean space and the caloric gauge
summary: Critical-regularity gauge theory on ℝ^d for a compact matrix group G: G-valued Sobolev maps at the critical exponent and their homotopy classes; rough connections with L^{d/2} curvature, d ≥ 3, and gauge invariance of finite energy; Uhlenbeck's lemma on balls and punctured balls for every compact G; the good global gauge theorem and topological classes; characteristic numbers by transgression, the Bogomol'nyi bound and the SU(2) instanton number; harmonic Yang–Mills connections on ℝ⁴ with regularity, decay, the Gursky–Kelleher–Streets energy gap and the ground state energy E_GS = 16π²/γ₀²; covariant elliptic and parabolic theory in homogeneous spaces; the Yang–Mills heat flow in the local caloric gauge with local well-posedness, convergence to flat limits and the Dichotomy and Threshold Theorems; the caloric gauge, the C¹ caloric manifold in ℋ, its tangent spaces and the nonlinear div–curl decomposition.

layers.title: Structure groups and pointwise gauge algebra

targets.name: YangMills.StructureGroup
targets.statement: A compact matrix structure group is (N, G, <,>) with G a closed subgroup of Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin N) ℂ, its Lie algebra 𝔤 = {X ∈ 𝔲(N) : exp(tX) ∈ G ∀ t}, and an Ad(G)-invariant inner product on 𝔤.
hypotheses: G closed in U(N), not assumed connected

api.name: lieSubalgebra
api.statement: 𝔤 is a real Lie subalgebra of the skew-Hermitian matrices, exp(𝔤) ⊆ G, Ad(g)𝔤 = 𝔤, and T_gG = g𝔤 = 𝔤g

api.name: ad_skew
api.statement: Ad(g) is an isometry and ad(X) is skew-adjoint

api.name: traceForm
api.statement: −Re tr(XY) is a positive definite Ad(U(N))-invariant inner product, so admissible inner products exist

api.name: idealDecomposition
api.statement: 𝔤 is the orthogonal direct sum of its centre and simple ideals

api.name: restrict_prod
api.statement: closed subgroups and block-diagonal products are structure groups

tests.name: su2_brackets

tests.name: adNotAd

targets.name: YangMills.nearestPointRetraction
targets.statement: There are an open neighbourhood 𝒰 of G in M_N(ℂ) and a smooth π_G : 𝒰 → G with π_G|G = id, π_G(M) the unique nearest point of G, and dπ_G(g) the orthogonal projection onto g𝔤.

tests.name: circleRetraction
tests.statement: G = U(1) ⊂ ℂ with ⟨z, w⟩ = Re(z w̄): on 𝒰, π_G(r e^{iθ}) = e^{iθ} for r > 0, so π_G(1 + i) = (1 + i)/√2 when 1 + i ∈ 𝒰, and dπ_G(1)(a + ib) = ib, the orthogonal projection onto 𝔤 = iℝ; a retraction with π_G(1 + h) = 1 + h − Re h fails π_G(𝒰) ⊆ G

tests.name: polarFactor
tests.statement: G = U(N): for M ∈ 𝒰, π_G(M) = M(M*M)^{−1/2}, the unitary polar factor, and dπ_G(1)(H) = (H − H*)/2; for M_t = [[1, t], [0, 1]] ∈ 𝒰 with t ≠ 0, π_G(M_t) = (4 + t²)^{−1/2}[[2, t], [−t, 2]] at squared distance 4 + t² − 2√(4 + t²) < t² = |M_t − 1|², so the Gram–Schmidt (QR) retraction, which sends M_t to 1, is not the nearest-point map (t = 1: 5 − 2√5 ≈ 0.528 < 1)

tests.name: finiteGroup
tests.statement: G = {±1} ⊂ U(1): 𝔤 = 0, π_G(z) = 1 for z ∈ 𝒰 with Re z > 0 and −1 for Re z < 0, so π_G is locally constant and dπ_G(±1) = 0, the orthogonal projection onto the zero space; the points with Re z = 0 are equidistant from ±1 and lie outside 𝒰

tests.name: noGlobalRetraction
tests.statement: G = U(N): |0 − g|² = tr(g*g) = N for every g ∈ U(N), so 0 has no unique nearest point of G and 0 ∉ 𝒰; no 𝒰 equal to the whole matrix space satisfies the statement, and every M ∈ 𝒰 is invertible

targets.name: YangMills.gauge_identities
targets.statement: For smooth A, O, O', B on open X ⊆ ℝ^d: O·A = Ad(O)A − O;x is 𝔤-valued, O·(O'·A) = (OO')·A, F[O·A] = Ad(O)F[A], [D_j,D_k] = ad F_jk, Bianchi, (OO');x = O;x + Ad(O)O';x, ∂_j(Ad(O)B) = Ad(O)∂_jB + [O;j, Ad(O)B]; and these are the SmoothBundlesConnections local formulas on X × G.

targets.name: YangMills.transgression

layers.title: The good global gauge and the topological class

gaps.title: L^p Neumann problem on the unit ball
gaps.detail: For 1 < p < ∞, d ≥ 2, f ∈ L^p(B₁) and V ∈ W^{1,p}(B₁;ℝ^d) with ∫_{B₁} f = ∫_{∂B₁} ν·V: Δu = f in B₁, ∂_νu = ν·V on ∂B₁ has a solution u ∈ W^{2,p}(B₁), unique up to constants, with ‖∇u‖_{W^{1,p}} ≤ C(d,p)(‖f‖_{L^p} + ‖V‖_{W^{1,p}}).
gaps.needs: PDE states elliptic boundary regularity only for the Dirichlet problem, and the method of continuity for Uhlenbeck's Coulomb gauge needs the W^{2,p} Neumann problem on the ball with inhomogeneous data.
gaps.section: Layer 5 (a new section on the L^p Neumann problem)

gaps.title: L^p div–curl estimate with vanishing normal component on the unit ball
gaps.detail: For 1 < p < ∞, d ≥ 2 and every 1-form a ∈ W^{1,p}(B₁;ℝ^d) with x^ℓa_ℓ = 0 on ∂B₁: ‖a‖_{W^{1,p}(B₁)} ≤ C(d,p)(‖da‖_{L^p} + ‖∂^ℓa_ℓ‖_{L^p}).
gaps.needs: PDE has no Gaffney-type estimate for the absolute boundary condition, and the a priori bound and uniqueness of Uhlenbeck's Coulomb gauge need it; it does not follow from the scalar Neumann problem alone.

gaps.title: Hardy's inequality on ℝ^d
gaps.detail: For d ≥ 2, 1 ≤ p < d, u ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d): ‖u/|x|‖_{L^p} ≤ (p/(d−p))‖∇u‖_{L^p}, extended to Ẇ^{1,p}.
gaps.needs: Hardy's inequality is at neither pin and in no roadmap section, and the terms [O_∞;x, b] with |O_∞;x| ≈ 1/|x| need it.

gaps.title: su(2) subalgebras realising γ₀ in compact Lie algebras
gaps.detail: Every noncommutative compact Lie algebra 𝔤 ⊆ 𝔲(N) with an ad-invariant inner product contains a Lie subalgebra 𝔰 ≅ su(2) with sup_{𝔰}|[X,Y]|/(|X||Y|) = sup_{𝔤}|[X,Y]|/(|X||Y|), through a highest root of a maximal abelian subalgebra and the sl₂-triple of the complexification (OhTataru-TopClass Lemma 6.4, lines 2381–2401).
gaps.needs: LieGroups Layer 6 states maximal tori but no root su(2) subalgebras, and the ground state energy needs one on which the bracket constant is attained.
